text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141. @
ALL PAPERS

- One energy company has already objected to a Thursday cabinet decision to set up a compensation programme related to the recent energy price hikes, based on contributions from the state and energy companies. Miklos Baron, head of German investor Bayernwerk's Hungarian office told Napi Gazdasag that the energy firms have not been consulted.
- Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy said the government had received a biased and incomplete briefing regarding the Budapest Bank's sales contract. @
- The fund management arm of Creditanstalt will shortly open two open-end funds.
- The Hungarian privatisation process will come to an end in 1997, said Privatisation Minister Judit Csiha.
- A new cargo facility will be built by the national airways Malev by late 1998.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn said in a wide-ranging interview that for him the essential thing is that left-wing policy should prevail in Hungary after 1998. @
- Trading in Fotex shares was suspended for 15 minutes yesterday after a price plunge from HUF 160 to HUF 121.
MAGYAR HIRLAP

- Gyorgy Szenasi, head of the international law division at the Foreign Ministry, denied a report that Hungary and Slovakia have abandoned efforts to reach an out of court settlement on the dispute over the Gabcikovo hydropower project.

- Most Hungarian companies are ill-informed about the process of the country's integration into the European Union, while many fear it, concluded a survey by the government's Workgroup for Integration Affairs. @
- The average yield of six-month treasury bills continued to decline at yesterday's auction.

- The Austrian electricity company Energieversorgung Niederosterreich yesterday denied reports that they plan to acquire stakes in the electricity distribution companies Edasz and Demasz from Electricite de France.

- Despite the increase in energy prices early this month, electricity and gas companies do not expect to see the profit, eight percent of their capital, promised by the state this year. Furthermore, the firms unanimously agree that they will be unable to carry out planned investments. @
- Hungary's largest microelectronics company has been established under the name Melcom Rt. through the merger of Intermos Rt and Interbip Rt.
NEPSZAVA

- President Jacques Chirac of France will announce in Parliament on January 16 when he visits Hungary that he will award the Legion d'honneur to President Arpad Goncz and 10 other dignitaries for their roles in the 1956 revolution.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- Hungarians bought convertible currencies worth $33.3 million last November, the National Bank reports. @
- Foreigners will be allowed to participate in the futures market of the Budapest Stock Exchange from January 24.
NEPSZABADSAG
- A recent study by 12 American doctors found that human rights are often violated in mental institutions, as those in care are kept in humiliating circumstances.

- Police captain J.Sz., head of a sub-department at the Szabolcs-Szatmar-Bereg County Police headquarters, has been taken into custody after investigations showed that he issued forged residence permits for Chinese people in return for cash.
-- Budapest newsroom (361) 327 4040
